- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap the immediate next period’s forecast at 1–2% below the peak.
- In cases where true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–3% on subsequent days.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤ 0.33), model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- If model forecast is significantly higher than recent 5-day average (e.g., > 10% above), reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates from model by > 3% in first 5 days, adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment is bullish, model should not be too bearish early on).
